subject: Pavel Nedvěd (Pavel Nedved)
title: Ballon d'Or, a golden goal and the little bear

lines.vo: Long blond mane, two nicknames, and no major trophy with Czechia?
lines.footage: Nedved long hair close-up in a 2003 Juventus match, slow motion

lines.vo: Pavel Nedvěd: a golden career, with one very unlucky golden goal.
lines.footage: Nedved celebrating a goal with fist clenched, Juventus era

lines.vo: Italian fans called him Furia Ceca. Czech fans called him Méďa, the little bear. A little bear with a lion's mane? Respect.
lines.footage: Nedved running at full speed with hair flying, Lazio or Juventus archive

lines.vo: The 1996 Euro final: lost to Germany on a golden goal. Big hair, bigger heartbreak.
lines.footage: Euro 1996 final highlights, golden goal moment, broadcaster logo removed

lines.vo: In 2003 he won the Ballon d'Or. The same year, a suspension kept him out of the Champions League final. Best player in Europe, missing the biggest game.
lines.footage: Nedved Ballon d'Or 2003 ceremony, clean award shot

lines.vo: He came out of international retirement for the 2006 World Cup. Czechia finished third in their group. Golden goal, golden career, bronze group stage. Pick your metal.
lines.footage: Czech squad at the 2006 World Cup group match, team photo

inserts.story: Setup: a stadium full of cartoon fans holding little bear plushies. Gag: a caricature Nedvěd's long blond mane whips across the pitch and blows a cartoon hat off a fan. Twist: the hat lands on a bear plushie, which tips it like a gentleman.
inserts.characters: Caricature of Pavel Nedvěd with long blond mane (no photo); generic cartoon fans

inserts.story: Setup: a 1996 scoreboard flashes 'GOLDEN GOAL'. Gag: a glowing golden ball rolls slowly past a caricature Nedvěd, who sighs and fixes his mane. Twist: the ball rolls into an empty trophy cabinet and stops right at the front, like it paid for the space.
inserts.characters: Caricature of Pavel Nedvěd (no photo); generic cartoon fans; generic cabinet

inserts.story: Setup: a cartoon group-table board for the 2006 World Cup. Gag: a caricature Nedvěd pulls his old boots out of a dusty box and they squeak. Twist: the board flips to show Czechia third, and a tiny bronze-coloured sticker peels off and sticks to his mane.
inserts.characters: Caricature of Pavel Nedvěd (no photo); generic cartoon board and boots

facts_used: Nicknames 'Furia Ceca' (Italian fans) and 'Méďa' (Czech fans), long blond hair - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Nedv%C4%9Bd
Euro 1996 final lost 2-1 to Germany on a golden goal - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Nedv%C4%9Bd
Ballon d'Or 2003; missed the Champions League final through suspension - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Nedv%C4%9Bd
Came out of international retirement for the 2006 World Cup; Czechia finished third in their group - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Nedv%C4%9Bd
91 caps, 18 goals for Czechia; 2002-03 Juventus season 43 apps, 14 goals - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Nedv%C4%9Bd
notes: Hair and nicknames are his public image, not health or family. The suspension line is the Champions League ban, not the Italian legal case (never mentioned); 'the same year' avoids claiming an order. Golden goal and 2006 group finish are from Wikipedia (high confidence). 'Bronze' and 'pick your metal' are jokes on a third-place group finish, not a medal claim. 'Italian fans / Czech fans' now matches the nickname source. The Prague marathon detail was left out (medium confidence only). Insert after_line values are 0-based.
